subject: Pilot charter: success metrics, guardrails & handoffs
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@opsync.ai>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:30:00Z
Subject: Pilot charter: success metrics, guardrails & handoffs

Thanks for the call today, Alex — great to meet you and the Opsync team. Per our discussion, attaching a first-pass pilot charter and the evaluation template so your engineering and product teams can map tests to success criteria. High-level recap and proposed next steps below.

Attachment stubs: opsync-pilot-charter-v1.pdf (charter + proposed KPIs), redwood-eval-template.xlsx (measurement workbook).

Proposed pilot scope
- Integration: Redwood hosted endpoint with API key + optional VPC connector for telemetry capture
- Workload: document ingestion -> retrieval-augmented generation for internal search use case
- Pilot duration: 4 weeks active testing + 2 weeks analysis

Success criteria (proposed)
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency <= 250 ms per request (95th across 2k sample queries)
- Throughput: sustain 45 QPS end-to-end for peak scenario (burst to 75 QPS for 2 minutes)
- Cost: token cost target <= $0.0009 per input+output token (measured across pilot)
- Quality: intent match >= 88% (automated classification against labeled set); human-annotator accuracy >= 4.1/5 on a 50-sample blind set; unacceptable hallucination rate <= 2%
- Reliability: error rate (5xx/4xx) < 0.5% over pilot window

Evaluation plan & ownership
- Opsync: provide canonical test corpus (500 labeled queries, production traffic profile, failure cases) — owner: Alex Turner
- Redwood: run weekly ingestion runs, provide continuous metrics dashboard and daily digest — owner: Priyom Das
- Joint: quality review cadence (weekly sync, mid-pilot checkpoint with sample blind eval) — owner: Aisha Rahman (Redwood) + Olivia Park (Opsync)

Proposed timeline
- Tue 2026-10-06: share charter + evaluation workbook (done — attached)
- Mon 2026-10-12: kickoff integration and keys; initial ingestion test by 10/15
- 10/19–11/16: active pilot testing window
- 11/17–11/30: analysis and final readout

Risks & guardrails
- Data sensitivity: recommend VPC connector and KMS for any PII; we will exclude logs beyond aggregated metrics unless you opt in
- Cost spikes: we will set burst limits and budget alerts; we recommend the $X/day cap during pilot

Please confirm the owners and timeline above or propose edits. Happy to lock down the kickoff time — suggested slot: Mon 2026-10-12, 10:00–10:30 PT.

Thanks,
Priyom
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@opsync.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia.park@opsync.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot charter: success metrics, guardrails & handoffs

Thanks, Priyom — got the materials and read through the charter. Quick clarifications:

1) Latency target — our internal SLAs for search are 200ms p95 end-to-end; is the 250ms number accounting for our retrieval layer + network roundtrip? If not, can Redwood target 180–200ms p95 for generation?

2) Quality metric — intent match is good; can we add an F1-style aggregate for entity extraction (they rely on named-entity accuracy)? We can share labeled entity set.

3) Data retention — we'll likely need audit logs for compliance; can Redwood provide a 90-day retention for request/response audit with role-based access?

We can confirm kickoff for 10/12 10:00 PT if those items look feasible. Olivia will coordinate the engineering team.

— Alex
Head of Platform, Opsync
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@opsync.ai>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot charter: success metrics, guardrails & handoffs

Alex — great notes. Short answers:

1) Latency: the 250ms was a conservative end-to-end target factoring minimal retrieval overhead. We can aim for 200ms p95 generation to accommodate your retrieval stack; Redwood will run an initial microbenchmark against your sample corpus and report a calibrated p95 by 10/10. Owner: Ben Carter.

2) Quality / entities: yes — please share the labeled entity set. We'll add an entity-extraction F1 target and include it in the evaluation workbook (suggested target >= 0.92). Owner: Aisha Rahman.

3) Audit logs: Redwood can provide 90-day request/response audit retention in the Private connector flow; for hosted we can provide aggregated logs and optional redact controls. We will outline the exact retention/role matrix in the kickoff docs.

Action items (owners)
- Ben: run microbenchmarks against sample corpus and post results to shared Drive by 2026-10-10
- Aisha: extend eval template with entity F1 sheet and scoring rules by 2026-10-09
- Alex / Olivia: share labeled entity set + canonical test corpus by 2026-10-09

I'll send a calendar invite for 10/12 10:00 PT once we confirm Alex/Olivia are available. Looking forward to getting started.

Priyom
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@opsync.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@opsync.ai>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot charter: success metrics, guardrails & handoffs

Thanks Priyom — confirmed for 10/12 10:00 PT. We've uploaded the labeled entity set and a 500-sample test corpus to the Drive link in the charter (see related_links). Ben and Aisha: Olivia here — our infra lead will sit in the kickoff and we expect to have API key access ready by EOD 10/12.

Noted on the bench and evaluation updates. If all goes well, Opsync will aim to convert to reserved capacity for Dedicated if the pilot demonstrates stable p95 and <1% error rate.

See you at the kickoff.

Olivia
Senior Engineering Manager, Opsync
